learning_outcomes.text: Recognize and understand the basic methodologies of linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithms; statistics, and optimization applied to engineering.
Solve, using mathematics and statistics, potential problems that may arise in engineering.
Recognize and understand the training needs that will be useful to successfully resolve new situations related to industrial engineering.
Propose creative solutions to satisfactorily respond to real needs and problems of society.
Develop professional texts and scientific-technical reports according to the conventions of the field of industrial technical engineering.
Adapt the organization of content and the use of language, verbal and non-verbal, to argue in various situations or before various audiences.
Apply industrial engineering knowledge to the learning of new methods and theories.
Show the advantages and opportunities of different solutions to the same problem critically and constructively.

syllabus_topics: Topic 2: DATA FITTING BY LEAST SQUARES
Residuals of a fit. Estimation of model parameters by least squares.
Trapezoidal rule. Midpoint rule. Simpson's rule.
Topic 4: NUMERICAL SOLUTION OF SINGLE-VARIABLE EQUATIONS
Probability. Conditional probability. Total probability theorem. Bayes' theorem.
Discrete and continuous random variables. Main probability distribution models.
teaching_methods: Problem/exercise solving in the ordinary classroom
Other methodologies (practical exercises using mathematical software)

assessment_methods.method: Mixed tests (two written exams, one per content block)
Other forms of evaluation (practical exercises using mathematical software)

assessment_rules: The final grade is based on two written exams (40% each) and practical exercises (20%). Both written exams are individual and in-person, consisting of problem-solving and theoretical questions. The practical exercises involve applying course content using mathematical software. Knowledge and understanding of the subject, correct use of mathematical language, and interpretation of results will be assessed.
